column1: # Japanese (ja) gap-filler catalog. Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
#   context  empty        a plain UI string; `source` is the English text shown by the code
#            @pattern     `source` is a template with {name} placeholders that match any text (a
#                         dynamic string such as `Undo {x}`); the placeholders are copied into the
#                         translation. Names n, k, i, pc, ms, fps, w, h ... and num* only match text
#   escapes  \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns.
#   lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# This file only fills gaps: strings already in ../../locales/ja.json (the call-site catalog) win.
# Clean-room: every entry was written from the plain meaning of the English label using ordinary
# Japanese computing and photography vocabulary. No proprietary localisation resource, string
# table or product UI was consulted or copied. Entries shared with the sister apps (same author,
# same vocabulary policy) were taken from their ja.tsv. Product and technology names stay in
# Latin letters; the trailing "..." / "…" of dialog commands is kept.
